issues.description: README diff drags in unrelated refactors — this is THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one
issues.detail: The README changes are not test additions. They rewrite StorageError.handle's signature (ex, req, resp, params -> req, resp, ex, params), swap str(code)+reason for falcon.code_to_http_status, change req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(), and reformat half the file. None of that belongs in a patch titled 'add POST request tests for things_advanced'. Submit the test additions on their own; submit the example changes on their own; submit the README reformat on its own. A diff that does three things is three diffs.

issues.description: StorageError.handle signature change in README is wrong-shape and contradicts Falcon's documented error handler signature
issues.detail: Falcon's add_error_handler passes (req, resp, ex, params) in newer signatures, but the README example previously matched (ex, req, resp, params) for a reason — it's the legacy signature still supported. Either way, silently flipping a signature in a README code block — with no test, no commit message rationale, no news fragment — is exactly the kind of drive-by 'while I'm here' edit that breaks people copy-pasting the example. If this is a real fix it deserves its own patch with its own justification.

issues.description: things_advanced.py change from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() is a behavior change disguised as a test fix
issues.detail: The PR description claims 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the actual diff swaps to bounded_stream.read() with no argument. Those are different APIs with different semantics — bounded_stream respects Content-Length and won't block on a misbehaving client; stream.read() reads until EOF. That's a legitimate improvement, but it's a separate change from adding tests, and the PR description doesn't match the diff. Either fix the description or split the patch. Bad commit messages waste the maintainer's time.

issues.description: FAQ example code has bad taste — special-cases zero-length when the framework already does
issues.detail: The PostTest class checks `req.content_length in (None, 0)` then separately does `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`. The `or 0` guard is dead code in the else branch because the outer if already excluded None and 0. This is exactly the kind of redundant special-case Torvalds means by 'bad taste' — write it so the special case disappears, or don't write the special case. Also, the example is missing a `:caption:` and the `assert(result.status == ...)` parens make it look like a function call; it's a statement. Style nit, but the FAQ is a teaching surface.

issues.description: Test assertions don't verify what the test claims to verify
issues.detail: resp4 asserts status_code == 400 for the empty-body-with-Content-Length-1 case, which exercises the JSONTranslator path. But the test doesn't distinguish between 'JSONTranslator caught empty body and returned 400' vs 'bounded_stream timeout' vs 'JSON decode error on partial read'. A good test for this regression would also assert the response body/title is the Malformed JSON or Empty request body error. Right now the test passes for the wrong reason as easily as the right one.

issues.description: Test uses magic Authorization value 'custom-token' that only works because _token_is_valid returns True
issues.detail: The example's AuthMiddleware._token_is_valid is `return True  # Suuuuuure it's valid...`. The test passes any string. Fine for now, but if anyone ever fixes the example's auth stub the tests silently break in a confusing way. A one-line comment in the test explaining 'auth is a stub in the example' would save the next maintainer five minutes.

issues.description: Hardcoded path '/1337/things' duplicated across tests with no shared fixture
issues.detail: Two new test blocks repeat the same URL pattern and most of the same headers. Not worth a fixture for two cases, but if a third lands, this becomes copy-paste sprawl. Note for the next patch, not a blocker for this one.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK, leaning REFUSE in current shape. The PR title says 'add POST request tests' but the diff includes a sprawling README reformat, a silent signature change to StorageError.handle, and a stream-API swap in the example — three or four patches mashed together. The actual test additions are reasonable but under-asserted (status code alone doesn't prove the right code path fired), and the FAQ example demonstrates the bad taste of a redundant special-case that the framework already handles. Split this into: (1) the example fix (stream -> bounded_stream) with its own justification and news fragment, (2) the README reformat/signature change as a separate intentional cleanup, (3) the test additions tightened to assert the failure reason not just the status, (4) the FAQ entry cleaned up. Talk is cheap; the diff has to do one thing and do it visibly.
